context.text: Jameis Winston is 17-6 to the Over in October in his career (since 2015) (+$945), going over the total by 4.8 PPG. That is the best mark of 52 QBs with at least 10 such games since 2015.
Since 1990, we've only seen 14 teams enter a season with a win total below 5 and end up closing as a road favorite. Those teams are 9-5 SU/ATS, with the under 10-4 in those games.
After the win last week against the Titans, John Harbaugh is 20-12 ATS since 2013 with a backup QB, including 11-4 SU in the first half when his team plays at home.
Jacoby Brissett has made 34 career road starts -- he has closed as a favorite just twice: 2022 as a Brown in Atlanta and in 2019 as a Colt in Jacksonville. His teams lost both games SU/ATS.
The Giants are 15-4 to the Under in the first four games of a season over the last five seasons (+$964), going under the total by 4.3 PPG. That is the best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
Home underdogs with Shawn Smith officiating are 13-3-1 ATS over the last three seasons (+$896), covering by 6.2 PPG. Fits this week: Giants.
The Cardinals are 0-5 ATS the week after facing Kyle Shanahan over the last four seasons (-$500), failing to cover by 7.0 PPG.
The Cardinals are 6-1 ATS against the NFC East over the last five seasons (+$451), covering by 4.0 PPG. Since leaving the NFC East in 2002, Cards are 32-17 ATS vs. their old division.

Cardinals are the 7th team since 2010 to enter regular season with win total under 6 and play b2b divisional games within first four weeks of regular season. Those teams are 1-5 SU and 2-4 ATS after that divisional stretch, losing by 8.5 PPG.
It is no shock to anyone that Jacoby Brissett and Jameis Winston have faced off just once in their careers. The O/U was 46.5 and the Colts and Bucs combined for 72 total pts that day.

The Saints are 3-15-1 ATS in primetime (6p ET or later) since 2020 (-$1,212), failing to cover by 5.0 PPG. Saints haven't covered in primetime since 2022 vs Bucs.

At home in New Orleans, the Saints have lost 9 consecutive games ATS in primetime, with their last cover coming in 2019 (and 7 consecutive games SU).

The 9-game ATS losing streak at home in primetime is tied for the 2nd-longest in the Super Bowl era:
12: Rams (1989-02)
9: Saints (2020-26)
9: Cardinals (2012-16)
The Falcons are 4-17 ATS in their 2nd straight road game over the last decade (-$1,331), failing to cover by 7.4 PPG. That is the worst mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
The Saints are 1-8 against the first-half spread at home since the start of last season (-$780).
Michael Penix Jr. is 0-4 ATS against the NFC South in his career (since 2024) (-$400), failing to cover by 14.1 PPG.

The Saints are 0-4 ATS at home with Land Clark officiating since 2022 (-$400), failing to cover by 10.9 PPG. Home teams with Land Clark officiating are 18-34 straight up over the last four seasons (-$2,062). Fits this week: Saints, Falcons.
The Saints are 5-0 to the Under on Mondays over the last five seasons (+$455), going under the total by 5.9 PPG.
The Saints are 16-8 to the Under against the NFC South over the last five seasons (+$655). That is the best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
Saints lost their home game last season vs Falcons, losing 24-10 as a 1.5-pt favorite. You have to go back to 2001-02 for the last time the Saints lost consecutive home games to the Falcons.

This is Kevin Stefanski's 7th season as a head coach in the NFL. He has never finished a season above .500 ATS on the road.

In the Super Bowl era, 103 head coaches have 50+ road games on their resume, Stefanski's 20-33-1 ATS (37.7%) mark is the worst.
So far this season, teams with a rest advantage are 7-3 SU and 7-2-1 ATS. That is the Falcons, Packers, Rams and Jets.
The Texans are 18-2 to the Under off an ATS loss over the last three seasons (+$1,436), going under the total by 5.3 PPG. That is the best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
Brian Schottenheimer and Dak Prescott as a QB-coach duo are 18-2 to the first-half Over together (since 2025) (+$1,580).
CJ Stroud is 1-10 ATS in the first four games of a season over the last three seasons (-$905), failing to cover by 4.4 PPG. That is the worst mark of 17 QBs with at least 10 such games in that span.
Brian Schottenheimer is 8-0 to the first-half Over as an underdog in his career (since 2025) (+$800).
Dak Prescott is 6-0 to the Over and 6-0 to the First Half Over against AFC opponents since the start of last season (+$545), going over the full game total by 7.5 PPG.
CJ Stroud is 11-4 to the Under against NFC opponents in his career (since 2023) (+$600). That is the 2nd-best mark of 35 QBs with at least 10 such games since 2023.
Dak Prescott is 6-2 ATS as an underdog since the start of last season (+$340).
Road underdogs with Brad Allen officiating are 4-18 straight up over the last three seasons (-$1,096). Fits this week: Cowboys.
The Cowboys are 9-2 to the Over indoors over the last two seasons (+$618), going over the total by 9.7 PPG. That is the best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
Teams coming off an International Series game as a road dog are just 10-21-1 SU (15-16-1 ATS), including 1-12 SU in their last 13 games dating back to 2018.

As an underdog, Dak Prescott is 6-2 ATS since start of last season. Dak's Cowboys have also scored at least 20 pts in ten straight games as an underdog (14 of their last 15 games as a dog).

In Dak's last 7 games as a dog, here are Dallas' point totals: 31, 30, 31, 24, 24 37, 40
Cowboys are on the road coming off an International Series game -- those teams are 17-27-4 on the second half moneyline in their next game.
The 49ers are 0-6 ATS against the AFC West over the last five seasons (-$600), failing to cover by 8.3 PPG.
The 49ers are 7-1 ATS with Ron Torbert officiating since 2020 (+$553), covering by 8.3 PPG.
Bo Nix is 9-2 ATS against NFC opponents in his career (since 2024) (+$617), covering by 9.3 PPG. That is the best mark of 25 QBs with at least 10 such games since 2024.
The Broncos are 4-0 straight up with Ron Torbert officiating over the last four seasons (+$565).
It even hurts the Broncos. Since 2020, Denver is 11-20 SU and 12-19 ATS going on the road after a home game.
Bo Nix has 11th fourth-quarter comebacks including the playoffs in his career, the 3rd-most by any QB in his first 3 seasons since 1950. Only John Elway (12) and Derek Carr (12) had more (via ESPN).
The Broncos have come back down 10+ pts in consecutive games against Rams and Jaguars. Last decade, teams to win b2b games trailing by 10+ pts in each are just 7-13 ATS in their next game.
Since start of last season, Broncos are now 5-3 SU in games when they are trailing by more than one possession at any point, the best mark in the NFL.

49ers have lost 9 consecutive games ATS at home vs. NFC West, with their last cover coming back in October of 2023 -- the longest such streak for any team since the Raiders between 2003-06 with 10.

When San Francisco faces a non-NFC West opponent at home, they are 9-3 SU and 8-4 ATS since 2024.
This will be Sean Payton's 11th total game as a head coach vs. 49ers. he was favored in the first ten (7-3 SU), with this being his first as an underdog.

From strictly an on-field results standpoint, Bo Nix has been a very different QB home vs road.

Home: 17-3 SU, 14-6 ATS | 18-1-1 in a 7-pt teaser
Road: 10-9 SU, 8-11 ATS | 16-3 in 7-pt teaser (2-10 ATS in his last 12 road starts)

Nobody believes in us. Since start of 2024, Bo Nix has started 20 games where the other team was receiving majority ticket support -- Nix and the Broncos are 14-6 ATS in those games, most profitable mark for any QB in that span.

The Panthers are currently on an 12-game ATS winning streak off a SU loss dating back to 2024. That is tied for the 3rd-longest ATS win streak after a SU loss (in same season) in Super Bowl era. 2022-25 Lions and 2011-13 Colts had a streak of 13 straight games.

After a SU win, Panthers are now 2-7 ATS since start of last season.
After last week, Bryce Young is now 9-12 SU (43%) when Carolina allows under 24 pts, which is tied for the worst win pct (min 20 gms) for any QB in the Super Bowl era.
Dating back to last season, the Lions are 0-6 SU/ATS in their last six games after a SU win.
The Panthers are 7-0 to the Under in primetime (6p ET or later) since 2020 (+$636), going under the total by 9.4 PPG.
Jared Goff is 13-3 ATS as a road favorite over the last four seasons (+$871), covering by 4.5 PPG. That is the best mark of 14 QBs with at least 10 such games in that span.
The Panthers are 4-0 to the Over with Clay Martin officiating over the last three seasons (+$364), going over the total by 12.0 PPG.
The Lions are 18-4 ATS on the road after a home game over the last five seasons (+$1,233), covering by 4.3 PPG. That is the best mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
The Panthers are 13-6 to the Over at home over the last three seasons (+$582), going over the total by 6.2 PPG.
Bryce Young has started three games in primetime with the Panthers (6p ET or later) and they are 0-3 SU, with Carolina scoring 17 pts or less in all three games.
Bryce Young has started 48 total games in his NFL career -- he has never closed with an over/under above 49.
Once cover kings: Lions haven't covered the spread in consecutive games since Weeks 2-5 of last season. Since then, they are 4-10-1 ATS in their last 15 games overall.

Neither the Packers or Bucs have won a game against the spread since Week 14 of last season. They are 0-14-1 ATS combined since then. Since Week 3 of last season, the Packers and Bucs are a combined 7-29-1 ATS -- a true someone has to cover matchup.

The Buccaneers have failed to cover the spread in 12 consecutive games, the longest such streak in the Super Bowl era by any team. Ironically enough, the Bucs also hold the longest straight up losing streak, dropping 26 straight games to start their franchise in 1976-77.
Favorites with Alex Kemp officiating are 26-10 ATS over the last three seasons (+$1,372), covering by 6.4 PPG.
The Packers are 2-9-1 ATS on the road since the start of last season (-$722), failing to cover by 3.2 PPG. That is the worst mark of any team in the NFL in that span.
Games officiated by Alex Kemp are 14-5 to the Under since the start of last season (+$773), going under the total by 7.7 PPG. Fits this week: Buccaneers, Packers.
Packers-Buccaneers games are 36-18 to the Under since 1980 (+$1,473). Fits this week: Buccaneers.

The Packers are 0-4 ATS against a backup QB since the start of last season (-$400), failing to cover by 7.0 PPG.

The Packers are 4-0 to the Over against a backup QB since the start of last season (+$364), going over the total by 9.5 PPG.
The Packers are 6-1 to the Under with extra rest (8+ days, no bye) over the last three seasons (+$445), going under the total by 12.8 PPG.
Last team to make the Super Bowl after starting the season 0-3 ATS? 1997 Packers -- who are the only team to do it in the last 50 years.

Tough game on TNF last week for Packers: Packers lost by 21 pts as a 4.5-pt favorite, faling to cover the spread by 25.5 points at home vs. Falcons -- worst ATS loss at home for GB since 2018. Green Bay starts the season 0-3 ATS for the first time since 2002.
Last three seasons, Jordan Love is 12-22-1 ATS as a starting QB, least profitable QB ATS in the NFL and the worst ATS win pct for any QB (min 15 starts) in that span.
Jordan Love has failed to cover 6 straight games dating back to last season. That is his longest such streak for a Packers QB since Brett Favre in 1997.

In the Super Bowl era, we had seen seven instances of a coach failing to cover the spread in ten straight games entering this year. They went 7-0 ATS in that 11th game. In Weeks 2 and 3, Todd Bowles made history by failing to cover both games. On to Week 4.
Jordan Love is a road favorite vs. backup QB, Jalon Daniels and Bucs this week. Going back to the end of 2024, Love has lost 11 consecutive starts ATS when receiving majority ticket support.

A little juice: Since 2005, 78 QBs have made their first career start within the first four games of the regular season -- they are 46-32 against the 1st half spread.

Jalon Daniels is trying to save the day. Only 8 teams since 2000 have entered the year at 50-1 odds to win it all or shorter, started 0-3 SU or worse and had to start a QB in their first start -- those QBs went 4-4 SU and 7-1 ATS, with all 8 covering a 6-pt teaser.
The Colts are 7-1 ATS in October over the last three seasons (+$551), covering by 7.4 PPG.
The Commanders are 9-2 to the Over with a backup QB starting since the start of last season (+$618), going over the total by 6.4 PPG.

Daniel Jones is 15-6 to the Under in non-conference games in his career (since 2019) (+$764). That is the 2nd-best mark of 43 QBs with at least 10 such games since 2019.

Daniel Jones is 2-12 ATS against NFC opponents over the last four seasons (-$1,021), failing to cover by 7.9 PPG. That is the worst mark of 34 QBs with at least 10 such games in that span.
Shane Steichen is 4-11 ATS against NFC opponents in his career (since 2023) (-$740), failing to cover by 4.4 PPG. That is the 2nd-worst mark of 35 head coaches with at least 10 such games since 2023.
Since 2013, we've seen 13 International Series games where at least one team started a backup QB -- the over is 10-3 in those games, going over the total by 3.6 PPG.
Dan Quinn and Marcus Mariota as a QB-coach duo are 5-0 to the Over at home (since 2025), going over the total by 14.9 PPG.
Marcus Mariota is 11-25-1 ATS in the full game spread and the first half spread the game after a SU win for his team, including 4-15 SU/ATS when that game is away from home.
Favorites have excelled in international games. They are 42-15-1 SU and 35-23 ATS, including 11-5 SU when both teams are under .500 SU entering the game.
Daniel Jones has faced a Dan Quinn-led team twice in his career as a starter, both with the Giants vs. Commanders. New York went 0-2 SU/ATS, both during the 2024 season.
The Bengals are 8-0 to the first-half Over as a favorite since the start of last season (+$800).
Trevor Lawrence is 12-4 against the first-half spread against AFC opponents since the start of last season (+$760). That is the best mark of 13 QBs with at least 10 such games in that span.
Teams covering by 10+ PPG on the season (minimum three games) are 47-72-3 ATS in their next game over the last 15 seasons (-$2,771). This week that includes the Jaguars, Raiders, 49ers and Vikings.

Joe Burrow is 8-3 ATS against the AFC South in his career (since 2020) (+$433). That is the best mark of 16 QBs with at least 10 such games since 2020.

Zac Taylor is 11-3 ATS against the AFC South since 2020 (+$707), covering by 4.6 PPG. That is the best mark of 11 head coaches with at least 10 such games in that span.
In six career games after facing the Steelers, Joe Burrow and the Bengals are 5-1 to the under in those subsequent matchups.

Trevor Lawrence has faced a Zac Taylor-led team three times as a starting QB, the Jaguars have lost all three games by 3, 3 and 4 total points, with Lawrence going 0-3 both SU and ATS in the 2nd half.
Not a sure thing: Joe Burrow has started 12 games at home off of a SU loss, he is 5-7 SU and 5-6-1 ATS in those games with just one cover since start of 2023 season.
Miami On Deck: Bengals travel to Miami to face the Dolphins next week. Teams with a road game to Miami on deck are just 15-26 ATS last 5 seasons, including 4-14 ATS in the last 18 games in this spot.

When two undefeated SU teams play in Week 4 or later, the home team is 26-16-1 SU and 25-17-1 ATS in the Super Bowl era. This is just the 2nd of these games since 2021, with Bucs/Eagles last year.

Home dogs in this spot are 9-6-1 SU and 13-3 ATS, covering by 7.6 PPG.
Kirk Cousins has won 7 straight games on the moneyline dating back to last season. That is his longest such streak since 2022.

Kirk Cousins is 8-0 to the Under against the AFC West since 2020 (+$727), going under the total by 7.8 PPG.

Krk Cousins is 10-1 to the Under against AFC opponents over the last four seasons (+$809), going under the total by 5.4 PPG. That is the best mark of 33 QBs with at least 10 such games in that span.
